notes: Two model families, same tasks, same graders, same repository state per task: Claude Code (claude-sonnet-5) and the OpenAI Codex CLI (gpt-5.6-sol, high effort). Four arms each, differing in one thing only. WITH: the workspace instructions document the dt CLI. MCP: generic instructions plus the repository's stdio design-system MCP server attached. MCP + POINTER: the MCP arm plus one line naming the server. WITHOUT: generic instructions. Each runtime reads the arm text from its own instruction file (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md).

Headline, replicated across both families: an MCP server is only as good as the pointer to it. Attached alone, Claude called it in 4 of 33 runs and Codex in 0 of 33, and design-system reuse stayed at the control's level (Claude 10 of 24 vs 12 of 24; Codex 4 of 24 vs 4 of 24). With one line naming the server, Claude called it in 31 of 33 runs and Codex in 33 of 33, and reuse rose to 21 of 24 in both, level with documenting the CLI (Claude 20 of 24, Codex 21 of 24). The clients defer MCP tools behind a tool search, so an agent that is not told the server exists rarely or never looks.
The pointer line, verbatim: "This repository's design system is available through the `design-system` MCP server; use its tools to find components and validate usage before finishing."

Pass rates saturated for both families. Eleven tasks, including three multi-component and cross-file tasks added to separate the arms (a tabbed settings panel with shared state, a filterable paginated directory, and a three-page migration off hand-rolled tabs). First-try pass is 31 to 33 of 33 for every Claude arm and 33 of 33 for every Codex arm. Today's differences are in how agents build, not whether they succeed. Tasks whose briefs say to use the design system correctly if used saw high reuse in every arm; compare arms within a task.

Isolation: Claude runs pass --strict-mcp-config and --setting-sources project,local; Codex runs use a throwaway CODEX_HOME holding only the login. Neither sees the operator's own instructions, skills, plugins or MCP servers.

Cost: Claude spend $95.13 including $28.19 on superseded runs (see supersededRuns: a stale hardcoded consumer list and a colour scan that flagged var(--color-white), both fixed and guarded in the selftest before re-running). Codex ran on a subscription, so it reports output tokens instead of dollars; token counts are not comparable across families.

Harness notes: a result-file name collision between parallel arms lost three Codex migration runs; filenames are now unique and the three runs were re-run from the same source commit. n=3 per arm per task per family. Treat per-task differences as anecdotes; the MCP call rates and the reuse gaps are consistent enough to read.
